why_criteria_not_names: A sample chosen by NAME after looking at the board is a sample chosen to agree. Each slot below is a SELECTOR evaluated against the board, fixed before any value was computed, so the sample cannot be steered toward transformations that happen to work. This is rule 10b's discipline applied to sampling rather than to a tolerance band.
spans: rule 12 names the shape: a top RB, a mid-round WR, an elite QB, a streaming DEF, a kicker, a deep flier. Extended to 13 so every transformation in the chain is exercised at least twice, and so the two positions with derived starter counts (RB/WR, which absorb the FLEX allocation) are sampled above AND below replacement.

selectors.rule: RB whose adjusted_adp is closest to 24 (mid-round RB)
RB nearest the replacement line: |proj_mean - replacement_points.RB| minimal
WR whose adjusted_adp is closest to 60 (mid-round WR)
WR nearest the replacement line: |proj_mean - replacement_points.WR| minimal
QB with the highest proj_mean (elite QB)
QB with the LOWEST positive vorp (the last QB worth starting)
DEF with the highest vorp (streaming DEF)
the player with the largest tier_drop anywhere on the board (a cliff)
deep flier: highest vorp among players with adjusted_adp > 120

transformations_to_verify: projection: proj_mean vs its authoritative sources (proj_sleeper / proj_fantasypros / proj_baseline) and the opportunity adjustment
replacement: replacement_points[pos] vs the LAST STARTER after iterative FLEX allocation
tier: tier / tier_rank / tier_size / tier_drop internal consistency
adp: adjusted_adp vs raw_adp under the keeper-shift and sequence blend
survival: P(available at my pick) from adjusted_adp and adp_sd
applicability_must_be_ARGUED: Any transformation marked not-applicable for a given player must state WHY in the output. Rule 12: the rule is otherwise satisfied by declaring everything inapplicable.
